doc_name: List of current members of the King's Privy Council for Canada
text: Members of the King's Privy Council for Canada are entitled to the title The Honourable, while Prime Ministers, Governors General, and Chief Justices are automatically granted the title The Right Honourable. Although Governors General receive the title The Right Honourable upon being sworn in, they are not inducted into the Privy Council until the end of their term, unless they were already members by virtue of another office. Other distinguished individuals, such as prominent former Cabinet ministers, may also be granted the title The Right Honourable. Leaders of opposition parties and provincial premiers are not automatically inducted into the Privy Council; opposition leaders may be added occasionally to mark significant events like the Canadian Centennial in 1967, the patriation of the Constitution, or to enable them to advise on national security issues under the Security of Information Act. Paul Martin introduced the practice of inducting parliamentary secretaries into the Privy Council, though this practice has not been continued by subsequent leaders. The Canadian Security Intelligence Service Act established the Security Intelligence Review Committee (SIRC), requiring its members to be drawn from Privy Council members who were not sitting in the Senate or House of Commons at the time of appointment; thus, individuals not already in the Privy Council were sworn in before being named to the committee. In 2019, the SIRC was replaced by the National Security and Intelligence Review Agency. Traditionally, the Order of Canada has been used to recognize prominent Canadians, but Brian Mulroney appointed 18 Canadians to the Privy Council on Canada Day in 1992 to commemorate Canada's 125th anniversary, and two additional individuals—W.O. Mitchell and Maurice Richard—were appointed later that year. Conrad Black, one of the 18 appointed, was expelled from the Privy Council in 2014 on the recommendation of Prime Minister Stephen Harper. This list details the longest-serving current members of the King's Privy Council for Canada.
